notes:
POC objective: validate dedicated capacity for latency SLOs (p95) and throughput guarantees under production-like load.

Key requirements (customer-specified):
- Chat (conversational assistant): p95 latency <= 200ms for short-turn (~64 token) responses; p95 <= 600ms for long-context (~2k token read + 128 token generation) in dedicated pool.
- Throughput: sustain 100 concurrent chat sessions with 60 RPS aggregate (estimate ~120 tokens/resp).
- Embeddings: bulk pipeline requires 600-800 qps sustained for 8h window (batching allowed).
- Reranking: 2k qps peak with sub-250ms tail for 8 candidate reranks.
- Soak: 48h continuous load test with representative diurnal pattern (spike at hour 13).

POC plan agreed:
- Phase 1 (synthetic baseline): run stepped load tests on dedicated 4xA100 equivalent to map qps->latency curve. Record p50/p95/p99 token-level latencies.
- Phase 2 (representative prompts): run canonical prompt set (50 prompts each for chat/long-context/embeddings/rerank). Include user prompt amplification and multi-turn context.
- Phase 3 (soak): 48h soak with mixed traffic (65% embeddings batch jobs, 20% chat, 15% rerank). Monitor KV cache hit rates and effective batching.
- Phase 4 (resilience): induce degraded conditions (1 GPU OOM simulation, 30% network jitter) to validate graceful degradation and fallback routing to lower-cost model variants.

Measurements of interest:
- p95 and p99 latency per model variant and per payload size.
- sustained qps at p95 SLOs.
- token cost per 1M tokens with/without prefix caching.
- effective autoscale times and cold-start behavior under burst.
- KV cache hit ratio and impact on tail latency.

POC notes from engineering calls:
- "We need guarantees for business-critical flows — a 5-minute outage would cost ~$17k/hr in lost ad auctions." (infra lead)
- Observed higher tail when >2048 token contexts combined with dynamic batching; Daniel recommended explicit route with smaller batch windows for long-context requests.

SLA negotiation points to resolve:
- Target uptime: 99.95% for dedicated pool; credits formula for degraded throughput vs complete outage.
- Latency SLA: p95 SLOs per workload class with measurement hooks in Redwood Console; define measurement windows and exclusion for scheduled maintenance.
- Capacity reservation: expectation of baseline reserved GPU count (8xA100 equiv) with burstable headroom; runway and lead time for horizontal scale.
- Security/compliance: contract appendix for KMS integration and monthly audit artifacts.

Open technical unknowns / risks:
- Long-context memory pressure and quantization interaction: need an extra run with q4_0 quantized model variant to validate memory and latency tradeoffs.
- Embeddings throughput when batching across heterogeneous length inputs — may need custom batching policy.
- Network topology (VPC peering) and egress policies lengthen provisioning time by ~2 weeks.

Next steps (owner mapped):
- Redwood (SE Daniel): finalize dedicated sizing runbook and test harness scripts by 2024-12-20.
- Palisade infra: provide sample S3 paths and KMS key ARN for POC by 2024-12-18.
- Schedule 48h soak window with SRE for 2025-01-08 to 2025-01-10.
- Legal/procurement: move from redlines to signature after successful soak and perf verification.

Short CRM-style summary: POC focused on throughput/latency guarantees for an enterprise adtech customer. Heavy emphasis on soak tests, reserved GPU planning, and clear SLA language. Procurement and SOC2 evidence are the main non-technical blockers.
